cells.tense: You are here at the closing edge, with the pen, and the closing is not a wall.
cells.act: open the door to the next thing on time, not early
cells.ask: Notice the next thing actually waiting on you, and walk through when its day arrives — not sooner.
cells.core:
You can let a stretch of your life finish without pretending it's still going. Something closes, your hands are steady closing it, and you're not tearing anything down to prove a point or keeping the lid on so it looks unfinished and safe. What's arriving next doesn't have to wait for the old thing to be mourned properly.

Notice the next thing actually waiting on you, and walk through when its day arrives — not sooner. That's the whole practice. Not a speech about turning pages, just the door opened at the hour it comes, empty hands going through. The cycle closes, you stand at the threshold, and the threshold is a place you can stand. That is what the completion is for.
cells.sheetLine: You can close a chapter and still be standing at the next door.
cells.verb: arriving whole and letting go into the next becoming
cells.place: at the doorway where what is must fully end for what will to begin

cells.tense: The next chapter is being written in your head before this one has finished turning.
cells.act: let this moment be a fresh entry, not a continuation
cells.ask: Take what's here today as brand new, not as a step toward what comes after.
cells.core:
You're calling the arrival before the boat has docked. Something's still running — a stretch of your life, a commitment, a thing in the middle — and you've already named it finished in your head and moved on to what's next. From the outside, people can see the old thing still going, and you keep talking about it in past tense.

Take what's here today as brand new, not as a step toward what comes after. No verdicts on it, no filing it away, no measuring ground covered. What you're meeting now is not the start of the next thing, and it's not a ghost of the last one. It's what's here, and it hasn't finished yet.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that stopped being a door some time back.
cells.act: notice what is newly here, right now
cells.ask: Look at what's here now that wasn't here last year, and let it be a thing in itself.
cells.core:
The cycles you're inside keep refusing to close. You can feel the edges — a job, a relationship, a chapter — and you keep looking for what's next before this one has ended, because ending it would mean something you'd rather not look at. That search has its own momentum, and you keep running on it.

Look at what's here now that wasn't here last year, and let it be a thing in itself. Your attention is what needs feeding, not your effort. The moment has kept changing whether or not you were watching, and this is you watching. The door you stand at is already a different room, and you can just be in it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep searching for the next door while standing in a room.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room where the writing is going on without you.
cells.act: release it on purpose, not by losing it
cells.ask: Name a grip you still hold, then set it down deliberately — your hands will learn the feel of open.
cells.core:
You have let things end and did not mark it. A cycle finished — a phase of work, a way of being with someone, a chapter you thought was still open — and you've been behaving as if it's still going, or as if it was yours to keep. From the inside this feels like steadiness. From outside, people near you can name the ending on your behalf.

Name a grip you still hold, then set it down deliberately — your hands will learn the feel of open. Not a project, not an obligation: the grip. Choose something specific and release it on purpose, and watch what your hands do when they've let go. Release works better chosen than noticed later. Your hands will get used to it.
